questions.question: What is the most common transmission voltage in the Philippines?
questions.tutor: NGCP uses 115 kV and 230 kV as primary transmission voltages.

questions.question: What is the relationship between line voltage and phase voltage in wye connection?
questions.tutor: For wye: VL = √3 × Vph, with 30° phase shift.

questions.question: What is the relationship between line current and phase current in delta connection?
questions.tutor: For delta: IL = √3 × Iph.

questions.question: What is the power formula for balanced three-phase system?
questions.tutor: P = √3 × VL × IL × PF (for balanced loads).

questions.question: What is the purpose of a transmission line?
questions.tutor: Transmission lines carry bulk power from generation to substations.

questions.question: What is the main advantage of high voltage transmission?
questions.tutor: Higher voltage reduces current, hence lower I²R losses.

questions.question: What is the typical distribution voltage for residential areas?
questions.tutor: Primary distribution: 13.8 kV, secondary: 230/400 V.

questions.question: What is ACSR conductor?
questions.tutor: ACSR has aluminum strands around steel core for strength and conductivity.

questions.question: What is a transmission line surge arrester used for?
questions.tutor: Surge arresters limit overvoltages from lightning or switching.

questions.question: What is the effect of skin effect in transmission lines?
questions.tutor: Skin effect causes AC current to concentrate at conductor surface.

questions.question: What is corona discharge?
questions.tutor: Corona occurs when electric field exceeds air dielectric strength, causing hissing and violet glow.

questions.question: What is the sag of a transmission line?
questions.tutor: Sag is the vertical dip of conductor between two supports.

questions.question: What is the main cause of line sag?
questions.tutor: Higher temperature expands conductor, increasing sag.

questions.question: What is a distribution substation?
questions.tutor: Distribution substation reduces transmission voltage to primary distribution level.

questions.question: What is the typical secondary distribution voltage in the Philippines?
questions.tutor: Residential secondary voltage is 230V single-phase or 400V three-phase.

questions.question: What is the function of a distribution transformer?
choices: Step down primary to utilization voltage
questions.tutor: Distribution transformer steps down primary (e.g., 13.8 kV) to 230/400 V.

questions.question: What is the length of a typical distribution primary line?
questions.tutor: Primary distribution lines typically run from substation to load centers (few km).

questions.question: What is the difference between transmission and distribution?
choices: Transmission: bulk power, long distance; Distribution: local delivery
questions.tutor: Transmission moves bulk power over long distances; distribution delivers to end users.

questions.question: What is a tap changer in a transformer?
questions.tutor: Tap changer adjusts transformer voltage ratio under load or off-load.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a recloser in distribution?
choices: Automatically restore power after temporary fault
questions.tutor: Recloser opens on fault and recloses automatically; clears temporary faults.

questions.question: What is the typical spacing of distribution poles in urban areas?
questions.tutor: Typical pole spacing is 30-50 meters depending on conductor sag and terrain.

questions.question: What is a sectionalizer?
choices: Isolates faulted section after recloser opens
questions.tutor: Sectionalizer opens after counting fault current interruptions to isolate faulted segment.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a lightning arrester on a distribution line?
questions.tutor: Lightning arrester clamps overvoltage and diverts surge current to ground.

questions.question: What is the nominal secondary voltage for commercial buildings?
questions.tutor: Commercial buildings typically use 230/400 V three-phase or 230 V single-phase.

questions.question: What is the typical frequency of Philippine power system?
questions.tutor: Philippines uses 60 Hz (same as US, different from 50 Hz of Europe/Asia).
